newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says handset efficiency on target.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says handset efficiency on target.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said on Thursday it was on target in improving the efficiency of its Mobile Phones arm which had fallen into a loss in the first quarter of the year.
"Nokia Mobile Phones continued to improve operating efficiency as planned, partly driven by the development towards regional focus in operations," Nokia said in its third quarter interim report.
The unit's operating margins were consistent with the third quarter of 1995 before the division's infrastructure problems started, it said, but gave no profit breakdown by division.
Nokia did not estimate its market share, but said it had recorded strong growth in Mobile Phones sales -- 58 percent in July-September compared to the third quarter last year.
Nokia's January-September operating profit was still lower than in the record-year 1995 due to Mobile Phones' problems.
"The decrease ... is primarily attributable to the unsatisfactory performance of Nokia Mobile Phones during the first two quarters," it said.
Nokia said earlier that the division had a slight operating loss in Q1 and a slight profit in Q2.
In Q3, growth in demand was strong, particularly in Europe and Asia but competition remained strong with markets increasingly shifting towards digital technology, it said.
Nokia said its recently launched products had been favourably received but that overall inventories fell sharply in Q3 -- down 1.17 billion markka in just three months.
"The Nokia 8110 for GSM, the new PDC digital phone for the Japanese market, the first IS-136 TDMA phone and the Nokia 9000 Communicator have met favourable market response," the company said.

"In combination with other products, especially the Nokia 2110 and the Nokia 1610, Nokia now offers the most comprehensive product range in GSM technology, fulfilling the requirements of various market segments," it added.
Nokia said it had expanded the Asian interface for the new 8110 handset to include seven languages, planned to be available by the end of the year.
It expects to have its PCS1900 version of the Communicator available for the American markets in the second half of 1997.

Nokia's Telecommunications arm, which makes telecom infrastructure products, reported 26 percent year-on-year sales growth to 3.13 billion markka in the third quarter while margins declined slightly on Q2.
"Operating margins declined somewhat from the second quarter of the year but were still slightly higher than in the corresponding period of 1995," Nokia said.
The unit's sales increased at a somewhat slower rate than expected while its profits exceeded expectations, it said.

Nokia's heavily restructured General Communications Products unit also recorded growth when disregarding disposed operations, and net sales of continuing operations were up 26 percent year-on-year at 1.15 billion markka in the third quarter.
Nokia said it maintained its generally positive outlook for the rest of the year.
"With the divestment of non-core operations, Nokia has sharpened its focus in telecom related businesses," President and CEO Jorma Ollila said in the report.

Forecasting "continuously growing operator needs for increasingly complex integrated solutions", Ollila said Nokia was "well-positioned to capitalise on its experience and total competence in cellular networks and access networks to meet these needs."
